In their one-room home in a Kolkata lane, Simran had tried every option. Her mother's sewing orders had doubled after her father's accident, and there was no cousin free, no neighbour, no way to split the days. The theatre workshop was full-time for a month.

She sat on the bed with her friend Jaya, who'd come to help her decide.

"So you're not going," Jaya said gently.

"Not this year." Simran's voice was steady, but her eyes were wet. "If I go, Ma will fall behind, and we need the money."

Then she pulled out a notebook and wrote at the top: NEXT YEAR. Under it: apply in January. Ask the teacher for a recommendation. Save for the fee from tuition money. Tell Ma the plan tonight.

That evening, her mother read the page and held it for a long time. "Next year," she said. "I'll help you get there."

qa.q: How long was the theatre workshop?
How did Simran feel when she said "Not this year"?
qa.a: Simran felt sad and disappointed, eyes wet, but steady and clear about the reason.

qa.q: What else could Simran do this year to keep the dream alive?
qa.a: She could join a weekend drama group or practise scenes at home, so she stays connected to theatre until she can apply.

qa.q: How might Simran's mother have felt reading the page?
qa.a: Her mother likely felt moved and grateful, and determined to support Simran's plan for next year.

grounding: Shows a student choosing to skip a workshop when no option works this year, but writing a plan to apply next year with a parent's support.

"So that's it? You're not going?" Lakshmi asked, sitting on the steps of their building.

Pranav shook his head. "We tried everything. Appa's leg is in plaster, the hotel needs someone at the desk, and Chithi is away. The cricket academy's summer batch is six weeks, full days."

"Maybe they'll give you a later batch?"

"I asked. There's no later batch this year."

Lakshmi was quiet. "That's really unfair."

"It is," Pranav said. "But it's one year." He pulled out his phone and showed her a note. "Next year's trials: February. I'll ask Coach for a letter in December. And I'll keep practising at the ground on Sundays."

"You already wrote a plan?"

"Appa and I wrote it together last night. He said he'll drive me to the trials himself."

Lakshmi smiled. "Then it's not over. It's just later."

qa.q: How did Pranav seem to feel about missing the academy this year?
qa.a: Pranav felt disappointed and a bit wronged but calm, treating it as a delay rather than a loss.

qa.q: What else could Pranav do this year to be ready for the trials?
qa.a: Pranav could ask Coach for a simple practice routine to follow on Sundays, so the practice is focused.

qa.q: How might Lakshmi see Pranav's plan?
qa.a: Lakshmi first thought it was unfair, but seeing the plan Lakshmi feels hopeful, calling it just later.

grounding: Shows a student accepting that no option works this year and skipping a summer programme, while writing a plan with a parent to apply next year.
